summary: Harbor light on the government wharf at Lahaina, Maui: a 1840 lamp (date disputed), the 1905 wooden tower, the 1917 concrete tower the Coast Guard owns.

structures.note: Thirty-nine feet (11.9 m) per LHF. The tower plaque gives a 1916 dedication.
55 ft to the lantern and 60 ft above high water (USLHS; LHF). Replaced in 1917.
Light tower built on the rebuilt house of 1866; replaced in 1905 (LHF quoting the Hawaiian Gazette and the Board).

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed (LHF). Coast Guard property, maintained by the Lahaina Restoration Foundation. The US Lighthouse Society lists the light as not open to the public.

events.note: First Lahaina light, per LHF and the tower plaque. Disputed: the 1936 Lighthouse Service review places Hawaii's first light at Kawaihae in 1859, with Lahaina's coming after it.
The old house pulled down and a new one erected on the site; lamps altered to burn kerosene (LHF, quoting the Hawaiian Gazette).
Federal Lighthouse Service takes over Hawaii's aids to navigation; the Board describes the light as two kitchen lamps (1936 review; LHF).
New wooden pyramidal skeleton tower with a lens lantern. Start date disputed: 13 May 1905 (LHF, quoting the Maui News); 20 June 1905 (Board notice in the Maui News, 1 July 1905).
Fixed white between two fixed red sectors, one red and one green sector before (Board bulletin, Pacific Commercial Advertiser, 26 August 1905).
Thirty-nine foot concrete pyramidal tower replaces the 1905 wooden tower; the plaque dates the dedication to 1916 (LHF).
Changed from oil to acetylene; fixed red changed to flashing white (Lighthouse Service Bulletin, 1922).
Converted to solar power by the Coast Guard's Aids to Navigation Team in Honolulu, with LED lamps (LHF).
Damaged but survived the wildfire of 8 August 2023 that destroyed most of Lahaina's historic district (LHF).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1922 Bulletin entry says 'Lahaina, east coast' of Maui. LHF places the light on the western end of Maui, and the 1905 Board notices put it on the western shore and at the government wharf. Treated as an error in the 1922 entry; the light is on the west coast.

notes_for_editor: Read before publishing. Fact-checked 2026-10-28. Corrections: (a) the opening's footnotes for the concrete tower and Coast Guard ownership now cite LighthouseFriends; the 1905 notices do not say either. (b) The sentence about the 1840 light and whaling ships had no footnote and cited an unnamed 'local record'; it is now cited to LighthouseFriends. (c) 'Whaling port of the islands' is replaced with what the sources say: whale ships favored the port, 1820-1860. (d) The 1905 Board notice is dated 15 June 1905 (printed 1 July). (e) The 1922 Bulletin's 'east coast' placement is stated and noted as contradicted. (f) The roster citation now points to the place record (archives.uslhs.org/places/lahaina-harbor), which prints the same keeper lines. (g) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: its quotations are paraphrased; the 1866 Hawaiian Gazette and the 1904 Board description are cited as quoted by LighthouseFriends, not as read. OPEN POINTS, stated in the story: FIRST LIGHT (LighthouseFriends and the plaque say 1840; the 1936 review says Kawaihae 1859; not reconciled). START OF THE 1905 LIGHT (13 May per LighthouseFriends quoting the Maui News; 20 June per the Board notice). THE CONCRETE TOWER'S YEAR (1916 plaque dedication; 1917 per LighthouseFriends). WHARF END (eastward end per the June notice; seaward end per the August bulletin). CHARACTERISTIC (station record Fl R 4s; fixed red per LighthouseFriends for 1917; fixed white with red sectors per the 1905 Board; the current Light List entry 6-28460 was not read). RANGE (the 1905 notice gives 12 miles white and 7 miles red; the station record 7 nm). AKO'S 1917 SUIT AND 1930 CENSUS: LighthouseFriends only; check a Hawaii court or newspaper record before relying on them. 2009 SOLAR CONVERSION AND 2023 FIRE: LighthouseFriends only; check current status (open hours, damage, restoration) before publishing. The 'previous keeper' who refused the oath in 1893 is not named and is not linked to Kaukaia. No storm, wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the sources read, so the Storms chapter is omitted. No photos were sourced. SHAPE: five chapters for about 1,180 words is above the moderate band (2-4 chapters); left for the writer to decide whether to merge.
